Hospitalization rates within 90 days after vaccination were also similar for each treatment group in each study (study 1: LAIV, 1.2%; TIV, 1.4%; study 2: LAIV, 3.4%; TIV, 3.3%). A review of all hospitalization diagnoses demonstrated that, in study I, there were ten hospitalizations due to L.RT (e.g., pneumonia, croup, wheezing, bronchospasm; LAIV, n=6; TIV, n=4), five of which occurred within 90 days after vaccination (LAIV, n=2; TIV, n=3). In study 2, there were 18 hospitalizations due to LRI (LAIV, n=11; TIV, n=7), 15 of which occurred within 90 days after vaccination (LAIV, л-8; TIV, л-7). Relative efficacy In studies 1 and 2, the relative efficacy of LAIV versus TIV among children with a history of wheezing or asthma was consistent with that observed in the overall study cohorts.
